rendered:
Notes that apply to every strain:
- Viable counts were measured by plate count after each suspension was set to an OD600 of 0.1[1].
- LODs were reported only for P. aeruginosa and L. monocytogenes, and CD gave the lower LOD in both cases.
- Discrimination was tested across OD600 =0.02–0.2[2].
- The mixture experiments are the ones shown in Fig. 4[3]. Its caption names these strains: P. aeruginosa, E. coli, E. sakazakii, S. typhimurium, L. monocytogenes and S. aureus[4].
- Only E. coli and E. faecium infections appear in the patient sepsis serum samples, compared against healthy volunteers. All of the strains were also classified in spiked human serum (Fig. 5[5]b), but those were not patient samples.

1. P. aeruginosa
- Viable concentration: 9.2 × 10^7 CFU/mL[6]
- LOD: OD600 =0.0034[7] by CD and 0.0066[8] by UV–vis
- Concentration discrimination: full[9]
- In mixtures: yes
- In clinical sepsis samples: no

2. E. coli
- Viable concentration: 8.5 × 10^7 CFU/mL[10]
- LOD: none reported, for either CD or UV–vis
- Concentration discrimination: full
- In mixtures: yes
- In clinical sepsis samples: yes[11]

3. E. sakazakii
- Viable concentration: 7.6 × 10^7 CFU/mL[12]
- LOD: none reported, for either CD or UV–vis
- Concentration discrimination: full
- In mixtures: yes
- In clinical sepsis samples: no

4. S. typhimurium
- Viable concentration: 6.4 ×10^7 CFU/mL[13]
- LOD: none reported, for either CD or UV–vis
- Concentration discrimination: only partial[14]
- In mixtures: yes
- In clinical sepsis samples: no

5. E. faecium
- Viable concentration: 7.4 ×10^7 CFU/mL[15]
- LOD: none reported, for either CD or UV–vis
- Concentration discrimination: full[16]
- In mixtures: not among the strains named for the mixture figure. The paper says nothing more about it here; the supplementary mixture figures are not in this document.
- In clinical sepsis samples: yes[17]

6. L. monocytogenes
- Viable concentration: 7.1 ×10^7 CFU/mL[18]
- LOD: 0.0123[19] by CD and 0.0125[20] by UV–vis, both as optical density
- Concentration discrimination: full
- In mixtures: yes
- In clinical sepsis samples: no

7. S. aureus
- Viable concentration: 8.2 ×10^7[21] CFU/mL
- LOD: none reported, for either CD or UV–vis
- Concentration discrimination: only partial[22]
- In mixtures: yes
- In clinical sepsis samples: no
